rules.text: Change only what the task needs. Keep unrelated renames, reformatting, file moves and refactors out of the diff.
Don't add options, flags, settings, dependencies or features the task didn't ask for.
Before adding a helper or an abstraction, look for an existing one in the repository and reuse it.
Remove unused imports, variables, parameters and branches left by your change.
Follow the naming, error handling, imports and structure of the neighbouring code, and the repository's formatter and linter settings.
Add a comment only to explain a decision, a constraint or behaviour that isn't obvious. Keep docstrings in the length and style of those around them. Don't add comments that restate the code.
Add logging only for a concrete need, in the repository's existing style, and never log secrets.
Before changing existing behaviour, check its tests and history for signs that it is intended. Keep it unless the task requires the change.
Never delete or weaken assertions, broaden expected results, or skip tests to make the suite pass.
Add tests for changed behaviour where the neighbouring tests live, in their framework and style, reusing their fixtures. For a bug fix, add a test that fails before the fix.
Keep public signatures, defaults, return values, errors and formats compatible unless the task asks for a breaking change.
Add a changelog or release-note entry only when the repository requires one, in its location and format.
Write commit messages and pull-request descriptions to the repository's templates and rules. Describe what changed and what you ran, and claim nothing you didn't run.
Run the checks the contribution guide and CI require, and report the exact commands and results, including any you couldn't run.
Before finishing, check the changed files for generated files, lockfiles and temporary files that don't belong.
